item.title: Shangri-La Frontier: The Seven Colossi Gets Its First Trailer and Playable Demo
item.description:
Netmarble has revealed the first Shangri-La Frontier The Seven Colossi trailer made specifically for the game, shown at Tokyo Game Show 2026 on September 17 alongside the first playable demo the title has ever had.
It is the first game adaptation of Shangri-La Frontier, the web novel by Katarina that passed a billion cumulative views in Japan before the manga and the anime. Netmarble Nexus is developing it for mobile and PC.
The PV was produced with C2C, the studio behind the anime series, and it is hand-animated 2D rather than engine footage. It runs through the familiar cast, puts Wethermon the Tombguard on screen as the threat, and works in the game’s tag-battle combat and action sequences written for the adaptation. It closes on the silhouettes of the Seven Colossi the subtitle refers to — the Unique Monsters nobody in the original has managed to bring down.
It went up at a media showcase Netmarble held at its booth the same day, which also ran a live gameplay demonstration and played messages from the original creators and the anime voice cast.
The demo is built around one-handed play: hold the phone, tap and swipe with a thumb. Battles run on their own by default, and the input that matters is tapping a character to switch them in. When a boss winds up a big attack, a TOUCH! prompt appears over Sunraku’s portrait, and switching at that instant triggers a perfect guard — the whole defensive game sits on that one beat.
The demo opens against Wethermon himself, a samurai-shaped Unique Monster whose big attacks are built around weather, and it is not a fight you are meant to win that early. Lycagon shows up in the demo too.
Underneath the one-handed controls, Netmarble describes a tag-based collectible RPG: you build a line-up, and the strategy is in which pairs you bring, how their deck combinations fit together and how you chain attacks across a swap. The company says the game recreates the original’s world, its cast and its Unique Monster fights rather than inventing a side story, which is what separates it from the usual anime tie-in.
Netmarble opened a global teaser site for the game in July, with official X and YouTube channels attached, and the Japanese App Store listing is already live for pre-orders. What the company has not given is a release date or a list of regions: the game is described only as launching on mobile and PC, and the TGS demo is the only way anyone has played it.

item.title: King’s Raid RE:VERSE Opens Pre-Registration, and It Has No Random Gacha
item.description:
The rewards land once the game launches: the “A New Beginning” Kasel costume, 30 Fragments of Mystery, 4 Mystery Intimacy Boxes and 100 Rubies. There is still no release date.
King’s Raid ran from 2016 until March 2025, when every version — global, Korea, Japan, Taiwan, China and Thailand — closed on the same day. Masangsoft bought the intellectual property afterwards and is rebuilding the game rather than making a sequel: the world, the cast, the story and the core combat stay, with balance work and quality-of-life changes layered on top. The studio says the RE:VERSE subtitle is meant as reconnecting with that world and carrying it forward, and the name only became official on September 3.
The Steam page leads with a line that is unusual for a hero collector: “Collect the Heroes You Want – No Random Gacha”. Heroes are chosen rather than rolled for, and the money sits elsewhere — costumes, in-app purchases and the usual progression sinks. Combat is real-time and tactical, built on skill timing and positioning rather than auto-battle, with co-op raids and online PvP alongside the story.
It is also cross-platform: a PC client on Steam that links to a Google or Apple account, plus iOS and Android. Two closed betas have already run, the second in April 2026, and the team has been publishing hero-by-hero balance notes ever since.
Masangsoft is showing the game at Tokyo Game Show 2026 with a standalone booth in Hall 1, 01-C06, built as an antique café based on May’s General Shop from the game, with photo areas dressed as locations from Orvel. It is the first time the relaunch has had a public showing of its own.
Masangsoft has not given a launch window, has not said which regions the relaunch covers, and has not detailed monetisation beyond the in-app purchases listed on the store page. Pre-registration and the beta feedback rounds are the only steps confirmed so far.

item.title: Solo Leveling: KARMA Gameplay Trailer Breaks Down Its Roguelite Runs
item.description:
Netmarble has released a Solo Leveling KARMA gameplay trailer for Tokyo Game Show 2026, published on September 17 on the game’s official channel, the same day the playable demo opened at Makuhari Messe. It is the first video the studio has built around the game’s systems rather than its story.
KARMA is Netmarble Neo‘s roguelite action RPG set during the 27-year Monarch War, the stretch of the original story that gets barely a mention. We covered the pre-registration that opened in Korea and Japan the day before the show.
Combat is a quarter-view hack and slash that reads a lot like an MMO at first glance. Skills come back after roughly five to ten seconds and there is no mana or stamina cost behind them, so once a skill is up you fire it. Enemy attacks draw their area on the ground before they land, and walking or dodging out of it avoids the hit entirely — but getting caught takes a large chunk of health, so reading the boss matters more than rotating your own buttons.
Progress inside a run is the three-cards-and-pick-one structure popularised by Slay the Spire, and the options are rolled fresh every attempt. You are choosing weapon traits and authorities — upgrades that either strengthen a skill or bolt an extra effect onto it — so a lucky pair of picks can change what a run is capable of rather than just its damage numbers.
Sung Jinwoo starts each run with most of his power stripped away and takes it back as he fights. His shadows come back with it: Igris and Beru return as screen-clearing ultimates that interrupt whatever the boss was doing, and you keep attacking while they are on screen.
The demo’s bosses pull from the original: Go Gun-hee blocks the way at one point, and monsters like the goblin that tears open a subway gate turn up as fights. Cha Hae-in appears as a boss as well, and beating her unlocks her as a playable character — the loop the full game seems to be built on. Choi Jong-in is also in the roster, and each character fights differently enough to change how a run plays.
Netmarble has confirmed PC, iOS and Android and a free-to-play model with paid items, but there is no launch window and no word on which regions get the game beyond Korea and Japan, where pre-registration is open.

item.title: FAREIDOLIA Is Playable for the First Time at Tokyo Game Show 2026
item.description:
FAREIDOLIA, the next game from the team behind Blue Archive, is playable in public for the first time at Tokyo Game Show 2026. The FAREIDOLIA playable demo runs at NEXON’s booth in Hall 7, C04 at Makuhari Messe from September 17 to 21.
It is the same game that spent months as Project RX; NEXON gave it its real name on August 24. It is made by the IO division of NEXON Games — the Blue Archive team — and runs on Unreal Engine 5.
NEXON describes an anime-style game built around three things: an immersive story, interaction with a distinctive cast, and lifestyle content rather than combat alone. The setting is Anima City, and the characters you live alongside are called Mates.
The home base is Tasogare Hall, and NEXON built it at full size for the show: the booth is a physical recreation of the building, with Minieh, Ohana, Shami and the Elevator Girl waiting inside, a trial-play corner and a rock-paper-scissors mini-game against whichever character you like most.
Alongside the demo, the game’s official channel published “Next Stop: Anima City”, an animated short that introduces the setting rather than the systems. The credits list WIT STUDIO among the animation houses on it, with Aimi Yamauchi directing and Chamakou on character design.
Combat runs on the Live Turn Battle system, where the turn order moves in real time and a boost gauge lets you push yourself up the queue, with skill animations far larger than the combat itself needs. Between the fights sit the character scenes, and an opening a good deal darker than the art on the booth suggests.
There is no release date and no final platform list. The demo at Makuhari is the whole of what is public, and NEXON has not committed to a window for either.

item.title: Pearl in Blue Shows Its First Gameplay at Tokyo Game Show 2026
item.description:
Netmarble put Pearl in Blue on stage at Tokyo Game Show 2026 on September 17 and played it live, which is the first Pearl in Blue gameplay anyone outside the studio has seen. Everything the game had shown until now was trailers.
The demo is playable at Netmarble’s booth at Makuhari Messe until September 21. There is still no release date, and we covered its previous trailer on September 12.
The concept Netmarble N2 keeps repeating is a monthly romantic comedy: the official site promises “a new story woven with her, every month”, set on Kenan Island, where the heroines live. Each month brings a new encounter, a new story and a new pearl — the game’s own term for what a heroine blooms.
Around that sit the parts that make it an RPG rather than a visual novel: pearls and blooming, Pearl Light, and the knights and their order, which is where the fighting comes from.
Pearl in Blue shares the booth with Shangri-La Frontier: The Seven Colossi and Solo Leveling: KARMA, which opened pre-registration in Korea and Japan the day before the show. Netmarble announced the three-title line-up back in July.
The concept trailer Netmarble put out for the show:
Netmarble has not given a launch window, has not confirmed regions beyond the Japanese service the site is built for, and has not said anything about monetisation. The TGS demo is the only way to play it so far.

item.title: Neverness to Everness 1.4 “For Whom the Verses Mourn” Arrives September 30
item.description:
The version was laid out in a special preview programme on September 16, and it follows version 1.3, which arrived on August 19 with Duskmoor, Zankou and Linko.
Blackbird headlines the first banner, and Akane Rin follows in the second half of the patch. Splitting a version into two character phases is how NTE has run its updates so far, so players saving for the second name have the whole first phase to keep pulling resources together.
The version preview programme, broadcast on September 16 at 19:30 (UTC+8), laid out the rest of the patch. The main story continues with a new episode, “The Witch”, and it comes with a side story, “To Us, Back Then”, which fills in the past rather than pushing the plot forward.
The bigger addition is a place: Pukaland, a new area built as a funfair, with the Pukaland Travelogue event running alongside it from September 30 to November 11 — the full length of the version. That is what the trailer is selling with its fairground of attractions and its promise that it will never, ever end.
Blackbird’s banner, “Foretold Finale”, opens with the version on September 30 and runs to October 21. Akane Rin takes over from October 21 to November 11. Both are limited S-Class, so a player who wants both needs to plan three weeks of income rather than treat it as one pull budget.
The trailer sells 1.4 as the noisy, festive end of a story arc — a fairground of attractions, a spell cast to make you smile, and the line that “it will never, ever end” over art that puts a crow, a stage and a school rooftop in the same frame. The version keeps the game’s own shape: an urban open world you drive around rather than a menu of stages.
That matters for anyone who came in through the vehicles: the city is still the point, and the new content hangs off it.
The official version PV is up on the game’s channel:
September 30 is the date given by the studio, with the usual maintenance window before the servers come back. Blackbird’s banner opens with the version; Akane Rin’s arrives in the second phase.
Guides, data and news for this game, all in one place.

item.title: Solo Leveling: KARMA Pre-Registration Opens in Korea and Japan
item.description:
Netmarble has opened Solo Leveling KARMA pre-registration in Korea and Japan, on the App Store and Google Play as well as the game’s official site. Sign-ups went live on September 16, 2026, a day before the game turned up as a playable demo at Tokyo Game Show.
The game is a roguelite action RPG built by Netmarble Neo on an official Solo Leveling licence, and it is not a version of the studio’s existing title. It fills in the 27-year Monarch War that the original story skips over: Sung Jinwoo winds time back to before the gates opened and fights the Monarchs again, alone, inside the Dimensional Gap.
Netmarble describes hack-and-slash combat in a quarter view, where swapping weapons changes the whole style of a run rather than just the damage numbers. The Shadow Monarch’s power summons shadows mid-fight, and the roguelite layer sits on the Monarch powers you pick during a battle, which rewrite which skills you have and how they look.
Bosses are the stated end point of each run, with pattern reading and hidden gimmicks rather than raw stat checks. The game is free to play with paid items, and the Japanese listing asks for iOS 16.1 or newer.
KARMA is one of three titles Netmarble took to Tokyo Game Show 2026 at Makuhari Messe, alongside Shangri-La Frontier: The Seven Colossi and Pearl in Blue. The booth demo puts players in the Dimensional Gap, which is the same setting the pre-registration campaign is selling.
A cinematic trailer went up on the game’s official channel on September 17:
Netmarble already runs Solo Leveling: ARISE, and the two are separate products: ARISE is the live action RPG with a hunter roster to build, while KARMA is a run-based roguelite where the build comes from what you pick inside a single fight. If you play ARISE, our Solo Leveling: Arise tier list ranks the hunters currently worth pulling.
There is no release date. Netmarble has not given a launch window, has not confirmed which regions get the game beyond the two where pre-registration opened, and has not detailed the monetisation. Pre-registration in Korea and Japan is the only step confirmed so far.

item.title: Mabinogi Mobile Release Date Confirmed: October 7 in Japan
item.description:
NEXON has set the Mabinogi Mobile release date in Japan for October 7, 2026. The date was announced during the game’s Tokyo Game Show 2026 special programme on September 17, and the game arrives on iOS, Android and PC (Windows) on the same day, free to play with paid items.
This is the Japanese service, and it is a separate launch from the Korean one: Mabinogi Mobile opened in Korea on March 27, 2025, so Japan gets it around eighteen months later. Both are built on the same world of Erinn that the original Mabinogi has been running in since 2005.
The official site files the game under a genre it calls a cozy online RPG, and the store listing spells out what that means in practice. Progression runs on level-up cards, and skills change according to the runes carved into them, which is how the game varies combat styles without locking you into one. Classes can be switched rather than rerolled.
Around the fighting sits the part the Mabinogi name is known for: fishing, cooking and gathering, campfire social scenes with dancing and instruments, and a deep wardrobe with dyeing so two players rarely look alike.
Pre-registration passed 200,000 sign-ups on September 15, which unlocked every milestone reward, and NEXON added a further tier at 250,000 that pays out ten Fashion Tickets. Registration stays open until 11:59 JST on October 7, the morning of launch, either through the app stores or with an email address on the official site.
The full announcement programme, with hands-on play ahead of the launch, is up in Japanese:
NEXON has not announced a Western or global service, and the October 7 date covers Japan only. The PC client is part of that launch rather than a later addition, which is the one detail that separates this version from a straight mobile port.

item.title: BanG Dream! Our Notes launches globally on September 24 with 1.5 million pre-registrations, releases song list and launch bonuses
item.description:
BanG Dream! Our Notes, the next-generation rhythm adventure in the Bandori franchise, will launch worldwide on iOS and Android on September 24, 2026, following the massive success of Girls Band Party, which has surpassed 20 million downloads since its 2017 debut. Published by Bilibili Game and Bushiroad Games and developed by FROMTOKYO, the free-to-play title features character gacha monetization and supports English, Traditional Chinese and Korean at launch.
The game centers on five girl bands competing in a fully voiced, story-driven campaign that blends hit-based rhythm gameplay with Live2D performances and exclusive band story chapters. Alongside returning acts MyGO!!!!!, Ave Mujica and Mugendai MewType, two new groups join the roster: millsage and Ikka Dumb Rock!, each bringing original songs and narrative arcs to the experience. A real-time multiplayer mode allows players to battle live against others, while a five-day cover song event kicks off at launch with daily new tracks.
The soundtrack blends originals from the BanG Dream! anime and real-life bands with a wide selection of high-profile covers. Confirmed tracks include Seishun Complex from Bocchi the Rock!, A Cruel Angel’s Thesis from Neon Genesis Evangelion, YOASOBI’s UNDEAD from the Monogatari series, Ao no Sumika from Jujutsu Kaisen and Vocaloid covers such as Six Trillion Years and Overnight Story. Several songs from the franchise’s “real” bands will also premiere in Our Notes.
Pre-registrations have exceeded 1.5 million globally, and all players will receive a complimentary Season 1 Mission Pass plus stars and gacha tickets as launch bonuses. A new trailer streamed on September 13 revealed the BanG Dream! Our Notes release date, song teasers and system overview, while a Japanese livestream special aired the same evening on the official Bandori YouTube channel. Pre-downloads begin on September 22, with the game going live on September 24 (UTC+9).
No version for Switch 2 or other consoles has been announced; Our Notes is currently exclusive to mobile platforms. At Tokyo Game Show 2026, Bushiroad plans to offer advance play sessions, Live2D performance screenings and novelty giveaways tied to the launch.

item.title: The CounterSide Reboot Has a Name: COUNTERSIDE: A [ANTEXILIAN]
item.description:
The reboot Studio BSide promised when CounterSide shut down has a name: COUNTERSIDE: A [ANTEXILIAN]. The studio opened an official account for the project on September 2, 2026, a week after the original game switched off its servers on August 26 following six years of service.
The account describes the game in four words — a “hardboiled urban lane battler” — which is the clearest signal so far that the CounterSide reboot keeps the real-time lane combat the original was built on, rather than starting from a different genre.
Very little, and the studio has not pretended otherwise. The channel has published three posts: the announcement art with the new logo, a follow-up teaser, and the account itself. There is no platform list, no gameplay footage and no release window. Studio BSide says both will be announced through the project’s own channels.
The announcement illustration puts faces from the original in front of a capital ship, which is as close as the studio has come to saying how much of the old game carries over. The second post, from September 9, is a single line in Korean, Japanese and English: “Do you remember? The day all of our administration failed.”
CounterSide ran for six years before closing on August 26, and the studio committed to a reboot in the same announcement that confirmed the shutdown. Its other live title is Star Savior, the 3D RPG it launched globally in March 2026, so the CounterSide reboot will be the studio’s second live game rather than its only one.
Platforms and a release window are the two details still missing, and Studio BSide has not said when either will arrive.
